findings.title: Backup-code login bypasses password and IdP checks when totpCode is supplied
findings.body: The new backup-code branch only checks credentials.backupCode. The existing password guard at line 121 runs only when !credentials.totpCode, and the identity-provider guards at lines 113 and 117 are also skipped when totpCode is truthy. An attacker who obtains a valid backup code can submit email, backupCode, and any non-empty totpCode; the request skips password and IdP validation, takes the backup-code branch, consumes the code, and authenticates the user. A single leaked backup code is therefore enough for account takeover. Require password or an equivalent trusted first-factor proof for the backup-code path and do not let an arbitrary totpCode value disable the earlier checks.

findings.title: Backup-code consumption is racy and permits replay or reinstatement
findings.body: The branch reads the encrypted backup-code list, sets one element to null, and writes the whole list back with no transaction, row lock, or conditional update. Two concurrent requests using the same code can both read the old list and both succeed, so a one-time code can be replayed. Concurrent requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's deletion and reinstate the other code. Use an atomic operation, such as a row lock plus verify-and-update or one row per hashed code with a usedAt conditional update, and add a concurrency test.

findings.title: Closing the backup-codes step by dialog dismissal skips onEnable and leaves UI stale
findings.body: After the enable API succeeds, handleEnable now only moves to SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes and no longer calls onEnable. onOpenChange at line 166 is passed straight through to Dialog, and onEnable is called only from the Close button at line 269. If the user closes with Escape, the X button, or the backdrop, 2FA is already enabled in the database but the parent is never notified; the settings switch can remain off and the user may try to enable 2FA again. Call the success callback when enabling succeeds and/or handle closing from this step explicitly.

findings.title: 2FA enable assertion does not actually validate the switch and ignores the new backup-codes step
findings.body: The added FIXME acknowledges that isChecked() passes even when the switch is not checked. With the new flow, after submitting the TOTP code the modal remains on the backup-codes step and onEnable/switch refresh does not happen until that step is closed. This test never closes the step, so the assertion is either false/flaky or, as the FIXME says, passing for the wrong reason. Use the data-state=checked assertion after closing backup codes, or otherwise explicitly complete the new step.

findings.title: No e2e coverage for backup-code login or one-time-use behavior
findings.body: The only new test interactions are downloading, copying, and closing the backup-code display. The TODO at line 12 explicitly defers backup-code login and disabling tests. The PR adds security-critical branches in next-auth-options and the disable endpoint, including single-use consumption, with no automated coverage. Add tests that log in with a backup code, assert the same code fails the second time, and disable 2FA with a backup code.

findings.title: Missing-backup-codes message is not actionable for existing 2FA users
findings.body: The new missing_backup_codes copy tells users to generate codes in settings, but the only generation path is the TOTP setup endpoint, which returns TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled once 2FA is enabled. Existing 2FA users with a null backupCodes column therefore reach a dead end from this message; they must disable and re-enable 2FA. Add an authenticated regeneration flow or change the message to reflect the actual recovery path.

findings.title: Password visibility toggle is removed from keyboard navigation
findings.body: Adding tabIndex={-1} to the password show/hide button makes the control unreachable by keyboard. Users who rely on keyboard navigation can no longer reveal the password they are typing, and this affects every PasswordField in the app. If the goal was to prevent focus stealing, use a visually hidden alternative or keep the button focusable.
